name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v1919: The vault manager brief needs one number before any of it is buildable - how many frames of each surface he has and which tab each is on - and a new indexer answers it from pixels alone with the inventory title and the active-tab gem, no model call. Over the 27 reels the sweeps already walk: 263 frames carry ownership evidence, 112 show his both-panels-open template, and 151 have a structurally readable stash tab across all five tabs. The archive is two archives - 883 loose frames and 1970 inside reels sharing zero filenames - and every stash measurement so far was taken on the loose half, which no sweep has ever walked. And the falsifiable prediction from v1912 came true: a pitch derived from three tabs placed the other two within two thousandths, so the gem reader is five of five, verified on his own footage. Widening the corpus surfaced a real miss and the ratchet went UP, which is what a corpus is for.
